## Loaded Stretch Training

Stretch training is commonly prescribed for improving measures of mobility and flexibility. However, evidence indicates that forms of stretch training may in fact mediate anabolic adaptations. For instance, research shows a hypertrophic benefit to dynamic training at long muscle lengths (i.e., stretched position) compared to training in a shortened position (52, 53). The mechanistic reasons for these findings remain unknown, but possibilities include heightened ultrastructural disruption, greater mechanical stress, or perhaps a combination of the two phenomena. Regardless of the mechanisms, a logical rationale exists for integrating stretch training into a resistance training program to confer an additive effect on muscle growth.
